source.text: Παῦλος ἀπόστολος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ διὰ θελήματος θεοῦ καὶ Τιμόθεος ὁ ἀδελφὸς τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ τῇ οὔσῃ ἐν Κορίνθῳ, σὺν τοῖς ἁγίοις πᾶσιν τοῖς οὖσιν ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Ἀχαΐᾳ·

records.literal_gloss: Paul, apostle of Christ Jesus through [the] will of God, and Timothy the brother, to the church of the God the [one] being in Corinth, with the holy [ones] all the [ones] being in whole the Achaia;

en.L: Paul, an apostle of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus through [the] will of God, and Timothy [our] brother, to the church of God that is in Corinth, with all the holy ones who are in the whole of Achaia.
en.B: From Paul, an apostle of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus by the will of God, and from Timothy our brother, to the church of God in Corinth, together with all God's holy people throughout Achaia.
en.R: This letter is from Paul and from our brother Timothy. It was God's will that I, Paul, should be an apostle, sent out by {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. We are writing to God's church in the city of Corinth, and to all of God's holy people everywhere in the province of Achaia.

fr.L: Paul, apôtre du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus par la volonté de Dieu, et Timothée [notre] frère, à l’église de Dieu qui est à Corinthe, avec tous les saints qui sont dans toute l’Achaïe.
fr.B: De la part de Paul, apôtre du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus par la volonté de Dieu, et de Timothée notre frère, à l’église de Dieu qui est à Corinthe, ainsi qu’à tout le peuple saint de Dieu dans l’Achaïe entière.
fr.R: Cette lettre vient de Paul et de notre frère Timothée. Dieu a voulu que moi, Paul, je sois apôtre, envoyé par le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} Jésus. Nous écrivons à l’église de Dieu qui est dans la ville de Corinthe, et à tout le peuple saint de Dieu, partout dans la province d’Achaïe.

es.L: Pablo, apóstol {{christos:de Cristo Jesús|del Mesías Jesús}} por [la] voluntad de Dios, y Timoteo, [nuestro] hermano, a la iglesia de Dios que está en Corinto, con todos los santos que están en toda Acaya:
es.B: De Pablo, apóstol {{christos:de Cristo Jesús|del Mesías Jesús}} por la voluntad de Dios, y de nuestro hermano Timoteo, a la iglesia de Dios en Corinto, junto con todo el pueblo santo de Dios en toda Acaya.
es.R: Esta carta es de Pablo y de nuestro hermano Timoteo. Dios quiso que yo, Pablo, fuera apóstol, enviado por {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}. Escribimos a la iglesia de Dios en la ciudad de Corinto, y a todo el pueblo de Dios en toda la provincia de Acaya.

sw.L: Paulo, mtume wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu kwa mapenzi ya Mungu, na Timotheo ndugu [yetu], kwa kanisa la Mungu lililoko Korintho, pamoja na watakatifu wote walioko katika Akaya yote.
sw.B: Kutoka kwa Paulo, mtume wa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu kwa mapenzi ya Mungu, na kutoka kwa Timotheo ndugu yetu, kwa kanisa la Mungu lililoko Korintho, pamoja na watakatifu wote wa Mungu walioko kila mahali katika Akaya.
sw.R: Barua hii inatoka kwa Paulo na kwa ndugu yetu Timotheo. Ni mapenzi ya Mungu kwamba mimi, Paulo, niwe mtume, nikitumwa na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu. Tunaliandikia kanisa la Mungu lililoko katika mji wa Korintho, na watu wote wa Mungu walio watakatifu kila mahali katika jimbo la Akaya.

decisions.choice: apostle: a messenger sent out with the authority of the one who sends him
alternatives: a missionary or church worker in general
decisions.reason: ἀπόστολος means one who is sent. Paul uses it for those commissioned by the risen Christ to speak for him, and counts himself among them (1 Corinthians 9:1; 15:7-9). In this letter his standing as an apostle is itself under attack (chapters 10-13), so the opening words "through the will of God" carry weight: the role was given by God, not claimed by Paul.

decisions.choice: church: the community of believers gathered as God's people
decisions.reason: ἐκκλησίᾳ was the ordinary word for an assembly of citizens. The Greek Old Testament uses it for Israel gathered before God (Deuteronomy 4:10; 9:10). "Of God" says whose assembly this is, as in 1 Corinthians 1:2. It means the people, not a place of worship.

decisions.choice: Corinth: the capital of the Roman province of Achaia, in southern Greece
decisions.reason: Paul founded the church in Corinth and stayed there a year and a half (Acts 18:1-11). Achaia was the province around it; it held other believers, for example at Cenchreae, Corinth's eastern port (Romans 16:1), and at Athens (Acts 17:34). The letter is meant for all of them.

decisions.choice: people set apart as belonging to God
decisions.reason: As in Philippians 1:1, ἁγίοις describes every believer, not a select few: the whole church is God's holy people, as Israel was (Exodus 19:6).

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: holy ones (L); God's holy people (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Philippians 1:1 and Colossians 1:2: in current English "saints" suggests unusually good people, not a whole congregation.

decisions.choice: It was God's will that I, Paul, should be an apostle, sent out by {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus
alternatives: an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God
decisions.reason: As in Colossians 1:1, Readable makes the opening a sentence, says what an apostle is, and adds "city" and "province" so that young readers know what Corinth and Achaia are.

decisions.choice: "du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}", "le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}"; "{{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}" for "in Christ"; "Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}" at Balanced and Readable (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians: French cannot say "en Messie", so the span for "in Christ" covers the preposition, with the familiar "en Christ" as the default. Elsewhere the article stays outside the span, since "du Christ" and "du Messie" both read naturally; Literal adds it without brackets because French needs it.

decisions.choice: l’église de Dieu, lowercase, for the congregation at Corinth; les saints (L), le peuple saint de Dieu (B, R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets: the capital is kept for the whole body of believers, and here one congregation is meant. "Les saints" today suggests unusually holy people, so Balanced and Readable say who they are, as the English does.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}; {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}
decisions.reason: As in Romans and Galatians, every Christos is a reader setting. For "Christ Jesus" the default is "Cristo Jesús" and the alternative "el Mesías Jesús"; where a preposition comes before the title the span takes it in, because Spanish contracts "de el" and "a el" to "del" and "al" before "Mesías". This holds for the whole letter.

decisions.choice: los santos (L); el pueblo santo de Dios (B); el pueblo de Dios (R)
decisions.reason: As in Ephesians and Colossians: in everyday Spanish "santos" are canonised saints, while Paul means all believers, set apart as belonging to God (meaning decision). Literal keeps the traditional word.

decisions.choice: watakatifu (L); watakatifu wa Mungu (B); watu wa Mungu walio watakatifu (R)
decisions.reason: As in Colossians 1:2: Literal keeps "watakatifu" (holy ones). Balanced adds "wa Mungu" so that the word names God's people rather than unusually good people, and Readable says plainly that they are God's people, set apart as holy.

source.text: χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Grace to you and peace from God Father of us and Lord Jesus Christ.

en.L: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and [the] Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: May God our Father and the Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} show you grace and give you peace.

fr.L: Grâce à vous et paix de la part de Dieu notre Père et du Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.B: Grâce et paix à vous de la part de Dieu notre Père et du Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}.
fr.R: Que Dieu notre Père et le Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} vous accordent leur grâce et vous donnent la paix.

es.L: Gracia a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y paz de Dios nuestro Padre y [del] Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.B: Gracia y paz a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} de parte de Dios nuestro Padre y del Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}.
es.R: Que Dios nuestro Padre y el Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} {{plural_you:les|os}} den gracia y paz.

sw.L: Neema kwenu na amani kutoka kwa Mungu Baba yetu na Bwana Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Neema na amani kutoka kwa Mungu Baba yetu na kwa Bwana Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ziwe nanyi.
sw.R: Mungu Baba yetu na Bwana Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} wawape neema na amani.

decisions.choice: one source: God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ together
decisions.reason: A single ἀπὸ ("from") governs both names, so Jesus is named with God the Father as the one source of grace and peace, as in Paul's other greetings (Romans 1:7; Philippians 1:2).

decisions.choice: a greeting turned into a blessing
decisions.reason: Greek letters normally opened with a one-word "greetings". Paul replaces it with χάρις (grace), close to it in sound, and adds εἰρήνη (peace), the usual Jewish greeting. It is a wish and a prayer for God's favor and wholeness.

decisions.choice: Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: May ... show you grace and give you peace
decisions.reason: The greeting has no verb. Readable states it as the prayer it is, as Colossians 1:2 does.

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: Paul writes to the church in Corinth in the plural throughout. Every plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain), as in Romans, Galatians and Ephesians.

source.text: Εὐλογητὸς ὁ θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὁ πατὴρ τῶν οἰκτιρμῶν καὶ θεὸς πάσης παρακλήσεως, ὁ παρακαλῶν ἡμᾶς ἐπὶ πάσῃ τῇ θλίψει ἡμῶν, εἰς τὸ δύνασθαι ἡμᾶς παρακαλεῖν τοὺς ἐν πάσῃ θλίψει διὰ τῆς παρακλήσεως ἧς παρακαλούμεθα αὐτοὶ ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed [is] the God and Father of the Lord of us Jesus Christ, the Father of the mercies and God of all comfort, \v 4 the [one] comforting us in all the affliction of us, for the to be able us to comfort the [ones] in every affliction through the comfort with which we are comforted ourselves by the God.

en.L: Blessed [is] the God and Father of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort, \v 4 who comforts us in all our affliction, so that we may be able to comfort those [who are] in any affliction through the comfort with which we ourselves are comforted by God.
en.B: Blessed is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, the merciful Father and the God from whom all comfort comes. \v 4 He comforts us in every hardship we face, so that we in turn can comfort people facing any hardship, passing on to them the same comfort God gives us.
en.R: Let us praise the God and Father of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. He is the Father who shows mercy, and the God who gives every kind of comfort. \v 4 He comforts us in all our troubles. Then we can comfort others when they are in any kind of trouble. We can give them the same comfort God has given us.

fr.L: Béni [soit] le Dieu et Père de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, le Père des miséricordes et Dieu de tout réconfort, \v 4 qui nous réconforte dans toute notre détresse, afin que nous puissions réconforter ceux [qui sont] dans quelque détresse que ce soit, par le réconfort avec lequel nous sommes nous-mêmes réconfortés par Dieu.
fr.B: Béni soit le Dieu et Père de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}, le Père plein de miséricorde, le Dieu de qui vient tout réconfort ! \v 4 Il nous réconforte dans toutes les épreuves que nous traversons, afin qu’à notre tour nous puissions réconforter ceux qui traversent n’importe quelle épreuve, en leur transmettant le réconfort que nous recevons nous-mêmes de Dieu.
fr.R: Louons le Dieu et Père de notre Seigneur Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. C’est le Père qui a compassion de nous, et le Dieu qui donne toutes sortes de réconfort. \v 4 Il nous réconforte dans toutes nos difficultés. Alors nous pouvons réconforter les autres quand ils ont des difficultés, quelles qu’elles soient. Nous pouvons leur donner le même réconfort que Dieu nous a donné.

es.L: Bendito [sea] el Dios y Padre de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} el Padre de las misericordias y Dios de todo consuelo, \v 4 que nos consuela en toda nuestra aflicción, para que podamos consolar a los que [están] en cualquier aflicción por medio del consuelo con que nosotros mismos somos consolados por Dios.
es.B: Bendito sea el Dios y Padre de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías,}} el Padre misericordioso y el Dios de quien viene todo consuelo. \v 4 Él nos consuela en todas nuestras dificultades, para que nosotros, a nuestra vez, podamos consolar a los que pasan por cualquier dificultad, dándoles el mismo consuelo que Dios nos da a nosotros.
es.R: ¡Alabemos al Dios y Padre de nuestro Señor {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}! Él es el Padre que muestra misericordia, y el Dios que da toda clase de consuelo. \v 4 Él nos consuela en todos nuestros problemas. Así nosotros podemos consolar a otros cuando tienen cualquier clase de problema. Podemos darles el mismo consuelo que Dios nos ha dado.

sw.L: Abarikiwe Mungu na Baba wa Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Baba wa rehema na Mungu wa faraja yote, \v 4 anayetufariji katika dhiki yetu yote, ili sisi tuweze kuwafariji walio katika dhiki yoyote kupitia faraja ambayo sisi wenyewe tunafarijiwa nayo na Mungu.
sw.B: Ahimidiwe Mungu na Baba wa Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Baba mwenye rehema na Mungu ambaye faraja yote hutoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}. \v 4 Yeye hutufariji katika kila dhiki tunayokutana nayo, ili nasi tuweze kuwafariji watu walio katika dhiki yoyote, tukiwapa faraja ile ile ambayo Mungu hutupa sisi.
sw.R: Tumsifu Mungu, Baba wa Bwana wetu Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}! Yeye ni Baba anayeonyesha rehema, na Mungu anayetoa kila aina ya faraja. \v 4 Hutufariji katika taabu zetu zote. Kisha nasi tunaweza kuwafariji wengine wanapokuwa katika taabu ya aina yoyote. Tunaweza kuwapa faraja ile ile ambayo Mungu ametupa.

decisions.choice: a Jewish blessing of God: praise that declares him worthy
alternatives: a wish that God may be blessed
decisions.reason: Εὐλογητὸς opens the traditional Jewish blessing of God, familiar from the Psalms (Psalm 41:14; 72:18) and used again in Ephesians 1:3 and 1 Peter 1:3. The Greek has no verb; it is a declaration of praise. In most of his letters Paul goes on from the greeting to thank God for his readers (Philippians 1:3; Colossians 1:3); here he blesses God for what God has done for Paul himself.

decisions.choice: God is both the God and the Father of the Lord Jesus Christ
alternatives: God, who is also the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: One article ὁ covers both θεὸς and πατὴρ, so "of our Lord Jesus Christ" goes with both words. Paul can speak of "the God of our Lord Jesus Christ" (Ephesians 1:17), and Jesus speaks of "my Father and your Father, my God and your God" (John 20:17).

decisions.choice: the Father who is merciful and from whom mercy comes
decisions.reason: "Father of mercies" is a Hebrew way of saying "the merciful Father", in which the second noun describes the first. οἰκτιρμῶν is plural, like the Hebrew word for compassion; Jewish prayers called God by much the same title.

decisions.choice: comfort: consolation that also strengthens, giving courage to go on
decisions.reason: The noun παρακλήσεως and the verb παρακαλῶν can mean to urge, to encourage or to comfort. Here they meet suffering, so comfort is meant, but comfort that strengthens, not only soothes. The words come ten times in verses 3-7 and set the theme of the chapter. In the Greek Old Testament the same verb opens Isaiah 40, God's word of comfort to his suffering people.

decisions.choice: affliction: hardship and pressure from outside, including persecution
decisions.reason: θλίψει means pressure that crushes. Paul uses it for the trouble that comes on believers in the world, often from opponents (1 Thessalonians 1:6; 3:3). Verse 8 gives an example from Paul's own life.

decisions.choice: the purpose of God's comfort: to be passed on to others
alternatives: a result Paul happens to notice
decisions.reason: εἰς τὸ with the infinitive states purpose. God comforts Paul so that he can comfort others; the comfort is given to be shared.

decisions.choice: Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: comfort
decisions.reason: One English word for the noun and the verb at every level keeps the repetition that ties verses 3-7 together. "Comfort" is the plainest word for help given in suffering; the meaning decision says it includes strength.

decisions.choice: affliction (L); hardship (B); trouble (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the traditional word. "Affliction" is formal for modern hearers, so Balanced uses "hardship" and Readable "trouble". "Suffering" is kept for a different word in verses 5-7.

decisions.choice: the merciful Father and the God from whom all comfort comes (B); the Father who shows mercy, and the God who gives every kind of comfort (R)
alternatives: the Father of mercies and God of all comfort
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the Hebrew-style phrases (see the meaning decision) instead of copying their form.

decisions.choice: Let us praise
decisions.reason: "Blessed" said of God is church language; Readable says what the blessing does. Literal and Balanced keep "blessed", the form of the Psalms.

decisions.choice: le réconfort, réconforter, at every level (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: One French word for the noun and the verb keeps the repetition that ties verses 3-7 together, as the English "comfort" does. "Consoler" is the traditional word but says only the easing of grief; "réconforter" also says that strength is given to go on (m4). "Encourager" is kept for other contexts.

decisions.choice: la détresse (L); l’épreuve (B); les difficultés (R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: French "affliction" now means grief rather than pressure from outside (m5), and "tribulation" is church language. "Détresse" is used at Literal, as in Romans; Balanced and Readable use plainer words, as the English "hardship" and "trouble" do. "Souffrances" is kept for the different word in verses 5-7.

decisions.choice: consuelo, consolar (every level); aflicción (L), dificultad (B), problema (R)
decisions.reason: The comfort word runs through 1:3-7 and comes back in chapter 7, so it stays "consuelo / consolar" at every level; the meaning decision says it also strengthens. For the hardship word, Literal keeps "aflicción" as in Romans 5:3; "tribulación" is church language, so Balanced says "dificultad" and Readable the everyday "problema". "Sufrimiento" is kept for the other Greek word in verses 5-7.

decisions.choice: ¡Alabemos ...!
decisions.reason: As in Ephesians 1:3, the call to praise needs no ustedes/vosotros setting and includes Paul with his readers.

decisions.choice: faraja, kufariji (every level)
decisions.reason: The comfort word runs through 1:3-7 and chapter 7, so Swahili keeps one family, "faraja" and "kufariji", at every level. "Kutia moyo" (to encourage) would catch the strengthening the meaning decision mentions but would break the chain of repeated words.

decisions.choice: dhiki (L, B); taabu (R)
decisions.reason: "Dhiki" is the word Romans uses for this term (Romans 5:3), pressure and hardship from outside; Readable uses the everyday "taabu". "Mateso" is kept for the sufferings of verses 5-7, a different Greek word.

decisions.choice: Abarikiwe (L); Ahimidiwe (B); Tumsifu (R)
decisions.reason: As in Ephesians 1:3, which opens with the same words: Literal keeps the word "bless", Balanced the familiar form for praising God, Readable a call to praise that includes Paul with his readers.

source.text: ὅτι καθὼς περισσεύει τὰ παθήματα τοῦ Χριστοῦ εἰς ἡμᾶς, οὕτως διὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ περισσεύει καὶ ἡ παράκλησις ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Because just as abound the sufferings of the Christ to us, so through the Christ abounds also the comfort of us.

en.L: For just as the sufferings of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} overflow to us, so also through the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} our comfort overflows.
en.B: For as the sufferings of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} overflow into our lives, so our comfort also overflows through {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: We share in the many sufferings of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. In the same way, we receive much comfort through {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

fr.L: Car de même que les souffrances du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} débordent sur nous, de même aussi, par le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, notre réconfort déborde.
fr.B: Car autant les souffrances du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} débordent dans notre vie, autant notre réconfort déborde aussi par le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.
fr.R: Nous avons une grande part aux souffrances du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. De la même façon, nous recevons beaucoup de réconfort par le {{christos:Christ|Messie}}.

es.L: Porque así como los sufrimientos del {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} sobreabundan para nosotros, así también por medio del {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} sobreabunda nuestro consuelo.
es.B: Porque así como los sufrimientos {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} nos llegan en abundancia, también por medio {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} nos llega consuelo en abundancia.
es.R: Nosotros compartimos los muchos sufrimientos {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}. Del mismo modo, recibimos mucho consuelo por medio {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}}.

sw.L: Kwa sababu kama vile mateso ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} yanavyozidi kwetu, vivyo hivyo kupitia {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} faraja yetu pia inazidi.
sw.B: Kwa maana kama mateso ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} yanavyofurika katika maisha yetu, vivyo hivyo faraja yetu pia inafurika kupitia {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Tunashiriki mateso mengi ya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Vivyo hivyo, tunapokea faraja nyingi kupitia {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

decisions.choice: sufferings that come to Christ's people because they belong to him: a share in his own sufferings
alternatives: Christ's sufferings on the cross only
the sorrows expected before the end of the age
decisions.reason: The sufferings "overflow to us", so they are not only Christ's past sufferings but something Paul goes through. Paul speaks of sharing in Christ's sufferings (Philippians 3:10) and of completing them in his own flesh (Colossians 1:24): those united with Christ suffer as he did and because of him.

decisions.choice: to overflow: to be more than enough
decisions.reason: περισσεύει is repeated in both halves of the sentence: the sufferings overflow, and the comfort overflows in equal measure. Paul uses the verb often in this letter (4:15; 8:2; 9:8).

decisions.choice: gives the reason for verse 4: why Paul has comfort to share
decisions.reason: ὅτι ("because, for") ties this verse to the last: Paul can comfort others because, through Christ, the comfort he receives is as great as his sufferings.

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting. The Greek has the article both times, and Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: We share in the many sufferings of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}
alternatives: the sufferings of Christ overflow to us
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "overflow to us" means (see the meaning decision), and uses "many" and "much" for the overflow.

decisions.choice: mateso
decisions.reason: "Mateso" (sufferings) is kept for this word, apart from "dhiki" (affliction) in verse 4, as Colossians 1:24 keeps the two Greek words apart.

source.text: εἴτε δὲ θλιβόμεθα, ὑπὲρ τῆς ὑμῶν παρακλήσεως καὶ σωτηρίας· εἴτε παρακαλούμεθα, ὑπὲρ τῆς ὑμῶν παρακλήσεως τῆς ἐνεργουμένης ἐν ὑπομονῇ τῶν αὐτῶν παθημάτων ὧν καὶ ἡμεῖς πάσχομεν, καὶ ἡ ἐλπὶς ἡμῶν βεβαία ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν· εἰδότες ὅτι ὡς κοινωνοί ἐστε τῶν παθημάτων, οὕτως καὶ τῆς παρακλήσεως.

records.literal_gloss: And whether we are afflicted, for the of you comfort and salvation; whether we are comforted, for the of you comfort, the [one] being at work in endurance of the same sufferings which also we suffer, \v 7 and the hope of us [is] firm for you; knowing that as sharers you are of the sufferings, so also of the comfort.

en.L: But if we are afflicted, [it is] for your comfort and salvation; if we are comforted, [it is] for your comfort, which is at work in [your] endurance of the same sufferings that we also suffer. \v 7 And our hope for you [is] firm, since we know that as you are sharers in the sufferings, so also [you are sharers] in the comfort.
en.B: If we are afflicted, it is so that you may be comforted and saved. If we are comforted, it is so that you may be comforted too, and that comfort works in you as you patiently endure the same sufferings we also suffer. \v 7 So we have a firm hope for you. We know that you are partners in the sufferings, and so you are partners in the comfort too.
en.R: If we suffer troubles, it is for your comfort and your salvation. If God comforts us, that is for your comfort too. This comfort gives you strength to keep going patiently when you go through the same sufferings we go through. \v 7 We have a hope for you that cannot be shaken. We know that you share in the sufferings, and in the same way you share in the comfort.

fr.L: Or, si nous sommes dans la détresse, [c’est] pour votre réconfort et votre salut ; si nous sommes réconfortés, [c’est] pour votre réconfort, qui agit dans [votre] endurance des mêmes souffrances que nous souffrons nous aussi. \v 7 Et notre espérance pour vous [est] ferme, sachant que, comme vous avez part aux souffrances, de même aussi [vous avez part] au réconfort.
fr.B: Si nous sommes dans l’épreuve, c’est pour que vous soyez réconfortés et sauvés. Si nous sommes réconfortés, c’est pour que vous le soyez aussi, et ce réconfort agit en vous quand vous endurez avec patience les mêmes souffrances que nous. \v 7 Aussi notre espérance pour vous est-elle ferme. Nous savons que vous êtes nos partenaires dans les souffrances, et donc aussi dans le réconfort.
fr.R: Si nous avons des difficultés, c’est pour que vous receviez du réconfort et que vous soyez sauvés. Si Dieu nous réconforte, c’est aussi pour vous réconforter. Ce réconfort vous donne la force de tenir bon avec patience quand vous passez par les mêmes souffrances que nous. \v 7 Notre espérance pour vous ne peut pas être ébranlée. Nous savons que vous avez part aux souffrances, et que, de la même façon, vous avez part au réconfort.

es.L: Pero si somos afligidos, [es] por {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} consuelo y salvación; si somos consolados, [es] por {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} consuelo, que actúa en [{{plural_you:su|vuestra}}] perseverancia en los mismos sufrimientos que también nosotros padecemos. \v 7 Y nuestra esperanza respecto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} [es] firme, sabiendo que así como {{plural_you:son|sois}} participantes de los sufrimientos, así también [lo {{plural_you:son|sois}}] del consuelo.
es.B: Si somos afligidos, es para que {{plural_you:ustedes sean|vosotros seáis}} consolados y salvados. Si somos consolados, es para que también {{plural_you:ustedes sean|vosotros seáis}} consolados, y ese consuelo actúa en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} cuando {{plural_you:soportan|soportáis}} con paciencia los mismos sufrimientos que también nosotros padecemos. \v 7 Por eso tenemos una esperanza firme en cuanto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Sabemos que {{plural_you:son|sois}} compañeros en los sufrimientos, y así también lo {{plural_you:son|sois}} en el consuelo.
es.R: Si pasamos por problemas, es para que {{plural_you:ustedes reciban|vosotros recibáis}} consuelo y salvación. Si Dios nos consuela, eso también es para {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} consuelo. Este consuelo {{plural_you:les|os}} da fuerzas para seguir adelante con paciencia cuando {{plural_you:pasan|pasáis}} por los mismos sufrimientos que nosotros. \v 7 Nuestra esperanza para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no puede ser sacudida. Sabemos que {{plural_you:comparten|compartís}} los sufrimientos, y del mismo modo {{plural_you:comparten|compartís}} el consuelo.

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa tunapatwa na dhiki, [ni] kwa ajili ya faraja yenu na wokovu; ikiwa tunafarijiwa, [ni] kwa ajili ya faraja yenu, inayofanya kazi katika uvumilivu [wenu] wa mateso yale yale ambayo sisi pia tunateseka. \v 7 Na tumaini letu kwa ajili yenu ni thabiti, tukijua kwamba kama mlivyo washiriki wa mateso, vivyo hivyo [mlivyo washiriki] wa faraja pia.
sw.B: Ikiwa tunapatwa na dhiki, ni ili ninyi mfarijiwe na kuokolewa. Ikiwa tunafarijiwa, ni ili ninyi pia mfarijiwe, na faraja hiyo hufanya kazi ndani yenu mnapoyavumilia kwa subira mateso yale yale tunayoyapata sisi pia. \v 7 Kwa hiyo tuna tumaini thabiti kwa ajili yenu. Tunajua kwamba ninyi ni washiriki katika mateso, na hivyo ni washiriki katika faraja pia.
sw.R: Tukipata taabu, ni kwa ajili ya faraja yenu na wokovu wenu. Mungu akitufariji, hiyo pia ni kwa ajili ya faraja yenu. Faraja hii inawapa nguvu ya kuendelea kuvumilia mnapopitia mateso yale yale tunayopitia sisi. \v 7 Tuna tumaini kwa ajili yenu lisiloweza kutikiswa. Tunajua kwamba mnashiriki katika mateso, na vivyo hivyo mnashiriki katika faraja.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: the order and wording printed here
alternatives: a longer form that adds "and salvation" after the second "your comfort" and moves "and our hope for you is firm" into the middle of verse 6
decisions.reason: Manuscripts arrange the clauses of verses 6-7 in several ways. Many later manuscripts repeat "and salvation" in the second half of verse 6 and place the clause about hope earlier. The SBLGNT follows important early manuscripts in the shorter order. Each form says the same thing: Paul's sufferings and his comfort both serve the Corinthians. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the comfort is at work: it shows its power in them
alternatives: the comfort is produced in them by God
decisions.reason: ἐνεργουμένης can be middle ("is at work, is effective") or passive ("is worked"). Paul uses the middle of this verb for a power at work in people (4:12; Romans 7:5). Either way the comfort is active in the Corinthians as they endure.

decisions.choice: endurance: bearing up steadily under pressure
decisions.reason: ὑπομονῇ is the strength to stay under a load without giving way. It is not a mood but a way of holding on, and here it is the form comfort takes.

decisions.choice: salvation: God's full and final rescue
decisions.reason: σωτηρίας is God's saving work, completed when Christ comes (Philippians 1:28; 2:12). Paul's sufferings serve it because they come with his bringing them the gospel.

decisions.choice: partners: people who have a real share in something together
decisions.reason: κοινωνοί is the word for business partners (Luke 5:10). The Corinthians do not just feel for Paul; they themselves suffer for Christ, and so they truly share in his comfort.

decisions.choice: the ground of Paul's hope: what he knows about sharing
decisions.reason: The participle εἰδότες ("knowing") gives the reason Paul's hope for them is firm: a share in Christ's sufferings brings a share in his comfort.

decisions.choice: the sentence broken into four (B) or six (R)
decisions.reason: Verses 6-7 are one Greek sentence. Balanced and Readable break it where each clause can stand, keeping its order.

decisions.choice: partners
decisions.reason: As in Philippians 1:5-7, "partners" says that the Corinthians have a real share, not just sympathy.

decisions.choice: If God comforts us; a hope for you that cannot be shaken
alternatives: If we are comforted; our hope for you is firm
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who comforts, as verse 4 says, and says what a "firm" hope is.

decisions.choice: compañeros
decisions.reason: "Socios" sounds like business; "compañeros" says people who really share something together (meaning decision), and keeps the plain register of Balanced.

decisions.choice: washiriki
decisions.reason: "Washiriki" (sharers, partners) says that they have a real share in both the sufferings and the comfort, and it is the word Swahili uses for fellowship and sharing.

source.text: Οὐ γὰρ θέλομεν ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, ὑπὲρ τῆς θλίψεως ἡμῶν τῆς γενομένης ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ, ὅτι καθ’ ὑπερβολὴν ὑπὲρ δύναμιν ἐβαρήθημεν, ὥστε ἐξαπορηθῆναι ἡμᾶς καὶ τοῦ ζῆν·

records.literal_gloss: For not we want you to be ignorant, brothers, about the affliction of us the [one] having happened in the Asia, that according to excess beyond power we were weighed down, so that to despair us even of the to live;

en.L: For we do not want you to be unaware, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, of our affliction that happened in Asia, that we were weighed down beyond measure, beyond [our] strength, so that we despaired even of living.
en.B: We do not want you to be left unaware, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, of the hardship that came on us in Asia. We were weighed down so heavily, so far past our strength, that we had given up hope even of staying alive.
en.R: We want you to know, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, about the terrible trouble we had in the province of Asia. The load we had to carry was far too heavy for us. It was so bad that we did not think we would live.

fr.L: Car nous ne voulons pas que vous ignoriez, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, notre détresse survenue en Asie : nous avons été accablés à l’excès, au-delà de [nos] forces, au point de désespérer même de vivre.
fr.B: Nous ne voulons pas vous laisser dans l’ignorance, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, au sujet de l’épreuve qui nous est arrivée en Asie. Nous avons été écrasés d’un poids si lourd, si loin au-delà de nos forces, que nous avions perdu jusqu’à l’espoir de rester en vie.
fr.R: Nous voulons que vous sachiez, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, quelles terribles difficultés nous avons eues dans la province d’Asie. Ce que nous avions à porter était beaucoup trop lourd pour nous. C’était si grave que nous ne pensions pas rester en vie.

es.L: Porque no queremos que {{plural_you:ustedes ignoren|vosotros ignoréis}}, hermanos, nuestra aflicción que nos sobrevino en Asia: que fuimos abrumados en extremo, más allá de [nuestras] fuerzas, de modo que perdimos la esperanza incluso de vivir.
es.B: No queremos, hermanos, que {{plural_you:desconozcan|desconozcáis}} la dificultad que nos sobrevino en Asia. Estuvimos tan abrumados, tan por encima de nuestras fuerzas, que ya habíamos perdido la esperanza de seguir con vida.
es.R: Hermanos, queremos que {{plural_you:sepan|sepáis}} los graves problemas que tuvimos en la provincia de Asia. La carga que teníamos que llevar era demasiado pesada para nosotros. Fue tan terrible que pensamos que no íbamos a sobrevivir.

sw.L: Kwa maana hatutaki msijue, ndugu, kuhusu dhiki yetu iliyotupata katika Asia, kwamba tulilemewa kupita kiasi, kupita nguvu [zetu], hata tukakata tamaa hata ya kuishi.
sw.B: Ndugu, hatutaki mkose kujua habari ya dhiki iliyotupata huko Asia. Tulilemewa kwa uzito mkubwa mno, kupita nguvu zetu, hata tukakata tamaa ya kuendelea kuishi.
sw.R: Ndugu, tunataka mjue kuhusu taabu kubwa tuliyoipata katika jimbo la Asia. Mzigo tuliokuwa nao ulikuwa mzito mno kwetu. Hali ilikuwa mbaya sana hata tukadhani hatutaishi.

decisions.choice: a formula for introducing important news
alternatives: a complaint that the readers do not know
decisions.reason: Paul uses "we do not want you to be unaware" when he is about to tell his readers something they need to know (Romans 1:13; 1 Corinthians 10:1; 1 Thessalonians 4:13).

decisions.choice: Asia: the Roman province in the west of what is now Turkey, with Ephesus as its chief city
decisions.reason: Paul worked in Ephesus for over two years (Acts 19:10). He does not say what the affliction was. Possibilities include the riot at Ephesus (Acts 19:23-41), danger he calls fighting wild beasts (1 Corinthians 15:32), imprisonment or severe illness. The Corinthians knew; we do not.

decisions.choice: "we" here is Paul himself, perhaps with his companions
decisions.reason: The letter moves between "I" (1:15-17, 1:23) and "we". Paul often uses "we" of himself and his fellow workers, and sometimes of himself alone. Here the danger is Paul's own, though others may have shared it. The plural does not mean the Corinthians.

decisions.choice: fellow believers, women and men
decisions.reason: ἀδελφοί is masculine plural, the ordinary way to address a mixed group of men and women together.

decisions.choice: to be utterly at a loss, with no way out
decisions.reason: ἐξαπορηθῆναι strengthens a verb meaning to be at a loss. In 4:8 Paul says he is perplexed but not utterly perplexed, using these two verbs; here, in Asia, he was brought to the end of all hope, even of life.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: Paul writes to the whole church, women and men. "Brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: the province of Asia
decisions.reason: In current English "Asia" means the continent; Readable says that a Roman province is meant.

decisions.choice: passé composé for past events at every level (for the whole letter)
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: 2 Corinthians is a letter: Paul tells his readers what happened to him and what he did, and French uses the passé composé for that ("nous avons été accablés"), as Colossians and Romans do. The imperfect describes the state he was in ("nous avions perdu", "nous ne pensions pas").

decisions.choice: {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}} for the readers (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As in English, Paul writes to the whole church, women and men (m4); "frères" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in Romans, Galatians and Philippians, Spanish "hermanos" already includes sisters as well as brothers, so the English gender setting has no Spanish counterpart here.

decisions.choice: ndugu, no gender span
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means brothers and sisters in the faith, so Swahili needs no gender setting in this letter, as in Romans and Galatians.

source.text: ἀλλὰ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἑαυτοῖς τὸ ἀπόκριμα τοῦ θανάτου ἐσχήκαμεν, ἵνα μὴ πεποιθότες ὦμεν ἐφ’ ἑαυτοῖς ἀλλ’ ἐπὶ τῷ θεῷ τῷ ἐγείροντι τοὺς νεκρούς·

records.literal_gloss: but ourselves in ourselves the sentence of the death we have had, so that not trusting we may be in ourselves but in the God the [one] raising the dead;

en.L: But we ourselves had the sentence of death in ourselves, so that we would not be trusting in ourselves but in God who raises the dead.
en.B: In fact, we had accepted within ourselves that we were condemned to die. That was so that our confidence would rest, not on ourselves, but on God, who raises the dead.
en.R: Inside ourselves, we felt like people who had been sentenced to death. But that happened so that we would not trust in ourselves. Instead, we would trust in God, who brings dead people back to life.

fr.L: Mais nous-mêmes, en nous-mêmes, nous avons eu la sentence de mort, afin que nous ne mettions pas notre confiance en nous-mêmes, mais en Dieu qui ressuscite les morts.
fr.B: En fait, nous avions accepté au fond de nous-mêmes d’être condamnés à mourir. Il en a été ainsi pour que notre confiance ne repose pas sur nous-mêmes, mais sur Dieu, qui ressuscite les morts.
fr.R: Au fond de nous, nous nous sentions comme des gens condamnés à mort. Mais c’est arrivé pour que nous ne mettions pas notre confiance en nous-mêmes. Nous devions plutôt la mettre en Dieu, qui fait revivre les morts.

es.L: Pero nosotros mismos tuvimos en nosotros mismos la sentencia de muerte, para que no estuviéramos confiando en nosotros mismos, sino en Dios, que resucita a los muertos.
es.B: De hecho, ya habíamos aceptado en nuestro interior que estábamos condenados a morir. Eso sucedió para que no pusiéramos nuestra confianza en nosotros mismos, sino en Dios, que resucita a los muertos.
es.R: Por dentro nos sentíamos como personas condenadas a muerte. Pero eso pasó para que no confiáramos en nosotros mismos. Así confiaríamos en Dios, que devuelve la vida a los muertos.

sw.L: Lakini sisi wenyewe tulikuwa na hukumu ya kifo ndani yetu wenyewe, ili tusiwe tukijitegemea sisi wenyewe bali tumtegemee Mungu anayewafufua wafu.
sw.B: Kwa kweli, ndani yetu tulikuwa tumekubali kwamba tumehukumiwa kufa. Hilo lilikuwa ili tusijitegemee sisi wenyewe, bali tumtegemee Mungu, anayewafufua wafu.
sw.R: Ndani yetu tulijiona kama watu waliokwisha kuhukumiwa kifo. Lakini hilo lilitokea ili tusijitegemee wenyewe. Badala yake, tumtegemee Mungu, anayewafufua watu waliokufa.

decisions.choice: a sentence: an official verdict, here a verdict of death
alternatives: an answer from God, given in reply to prayer
decisions.reason: ἀπόκριμα is an official decision, and in inscriptions of the time it can be a ruling given in answer to a request. Paul says he had it "in ourselves": whether or not a court was involved, he had inwardly accepted that he was condemned to die. Some take the word as God's answer to his prayer, which was to trust God; the next clause gives that purpose in any case.

decisions.choice: the perfect tense: the verdict was received and still marks him
decisions.reason: ἐσχήκαμεν is perfect: the experience is past, but its effect remains. Paul writes as one who still lives under its lesson.

decisions.choice: God's purpose in the experience
decisions.reason: ἵνα states purpose: the danger served to turn Paul's trust away from himself to God.

decisions.choice: God who raises the dead: a title of God from Jewish prayer
decisions.reason: A daily Jewish prayer of the time praised God as the one who gives life to the dead, and Paul uses the same kind of title for God in Romans 4:17. Here it is personal: God raised Paul from what he took to be certain death, and he will raise the dead at the end (4:14).

decisions.choice: we had accepted within ourselves that we were condemned to die
alternatives: we had the sentence of death in ourselves
decisions.reason: Balanced says what having the sentence "in ourselves" means: an inner conviction (see the meaning decision).

decisions.choice: who brings dead people back to life
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what raising the dead is.

source.text: ὃς ἐκ τηλικούτου θανάτου ἐρρύσατο ἡμᾶς καὶ ῥύσεται, εἰς ὃν ἠλπίκαμεν ὅτι καὶ ἔτι ῥύσεται, συνυπουργούντων καὶ ὑμῶν ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τῇ δεήσει, ἵνα ἐκ πολλῶν προσώπων τὸ εἰς ἡμᾶς χάρισμα διὰ πολλῶν εὐχαριστηθῇ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: who from so great a death rescued us and will rescue, in whom we have hoped that also still he will rescue, \v 11 helping together also you on behalf of us by the prayer, so that from many faces the to us gift through many may be given thanks for on behalf of us.

en.L: who rescued us from so great a death and will rescue [us], on whom we have set our hope that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will yet rescue [us] again, \v 11 as you also help together on our behalf by [your] prayer, so that thanks may be given by many persons on our behalf for the gift [granted] to us through many.
en.B: God rescued us from so great a death, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rescue us. We have fixed our hope on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rescue us yet again, \v 11 as you also work with us by praying for us. Then the gift God has given us through the prayers of many will be met with thanks from many people for our sake.
en.R: God rescued us from that terrible danger of death, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rescue us again. We trust {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to keep on rescuing us, \v 11 and you are helping us by praying for us. Many people are praying. So when God is kind to us and answers their prayers, many people will thank {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done for us.

fr.L: qui nous a délivrés d’une si grande mort et [nous] délivrera, en qui nous avons mis notre espérance qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} [nous] délivrera encore, \v 11 vous aussi nous aidant ensemble par la prière en notre faveur, afin que, de la part de nombreuses personnes, grâce soit rendue à notre sujet pour le don [accordé] à nous par l’intermédiaire de beaucoup.
fr.B: Dieu nous a délivrés d’une si grande mort, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous délivrera. Nous avons placé en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} notre espérance : {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous délivrera encore, \v 11 tandis que vous aussi travaillez avec nous en priant pour nous. Alors le don que Dieu nous a fait en réponse aux prières de beaucoup sera accueilli par les remerciements de beaucoup de gens, à cause de nous.
fr.R: Dieu nous a délivrés de ce terrible danger de mort, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous délivrera encore. Nous comptons sur {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} pour continuer à nous délivrer, \v 11 et vous nous aidez en priant pour nous. Beaucoup de gens prient. Alors, quand Dieu sera bon pour nous et répondra à leurs prières, beaucoup de gens {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} remercieront pour ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} aura fait pour nous.

es.L: quien nos rescató de una muerte tan grande y [nos] rescatará; en quien hemos puesto [nuestra] esperanza de que todavía [nos] rescatará, \v 11 colaborando también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} a favor nuestro con la oración, para que, de parte de muchas personas, se den gracias a favor nuestro por el don [concedido] a nosotros por medio de muchos.
es.B: Dios nos rescató de una muerte tan terrible, y nos rescatará. En {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hemos puesto nuestra esperanza de que nos seguirá rescatando, \v 11 mientras {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} también {{plural_you:colaboran|colaboráis}} con nosotros orando por nosotros. Así, el don que Dios nos ha concedido en respuesta a las oraciones de muchos hará que muchas personas den gracias por nosotros.
es.R: Dios nos rescató de aquel terrible peligro de muerte, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos volverá a rescatar. Confiamos en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}: seguirá rescatándonos. \v 11 Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} nos {{plural_you:ayudan|ayudáis}} orando por nosotros. Muchas personas están orando. Así que, cuando Dios sea bueno con nosotros y responda a sus oraciones, muchas personas {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} darán gracias por lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha hecho por nosotros.

sw.L: ambaye alituokoa kutoka katika kifo kikubwa namna hiyo, na atatuokoa; ambaye {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} tumeweka tumaini [letu] kwamba bado atatuokoa tena, \v 11 ninyi pia mkisaidia pamoja [nasi] kwa ajili yetu kwa maombi [yenu], ili shukrani zitolewe na watu wengi kwa ajili yetu kwa karama [tuliyopewa] kupitia wengi.
sw.B: Mungu alituokoa kutoka katika kifo kikubwa namna hiyo, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atatuokoa. Tumeweka tumaini letu {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} kwamba atatuokoa tena, \v 11 nanyi pia mkishirikiana nasi kwa kutuombea. Ndipo karama ambayo Mungu ametupa kwa sababu ya maombi ya wengi itapokelewa kwa shukrani za watu wengi kwa ajili yetu.
sw.R: Mungu alituokoa kutoka katika hatari ile mbaya ya kifo, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} atatuokoa tena. Tunamtumaini kwamba ataendelea kutuokoa, \v 11 nanyi mnatusaidia kwa kutuombea. Watu wengi wanaomba. Kwa hiyo Mungu atakapotufanyia wema na kujibu maombi yao, watu wengi watamshukuru kwa yale aliyotufanyia.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "so great a death" and "and will rescue"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ here. Some have the present "and rescues", some leave the words out, perhaps because the repeated "will rescue" seemed redundant, and an early papyrus has the plural "deaths". The SBLGNT follows important early manuscripts. The meaning is much the same. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: past, future and continuing rescue: God's rescue in Asia gives a settled hope
decisions.reason: ἐρρύσατο is past, the event in Asia; ῥύσεται looks ahead; ἠλπίκαμεν is perfect, a hope set once and still held, that God "will yet" rescue. The repetition is deliberate: what God did, he will do.

decisions.choice: the Corinthians' prayer goes along with God's rescue
alternatives: a condition: God will rescue only if they pray
decisions.reason: συνυπουργούντων is a participle phrase, "you also helping together". It describes the Corinthians' share in Paul's rescue without making it a strict condition. Paul often asks for prayer as real help (Romans 15:30; Philippians 1:19).

decisions.choice: many persons
alternatives: many faces turned up to God in prayer
decisions.reason: προσώπων means "face" and could also mean "person" in Greek of the time. "From many faces" means from many people. Some see a picture of faces lifted in prayer, but the plain sense is enough.

decisions.choice: a gift of God's grace: here, God's rescue of Paul
alternatives: a spiritual ability given to a believer
decisions.reason: χάρισμα is a gift that comes from God's grace. In 1 Corinthians 12 the word is used for gifts of the Spirit; here the gift is Paul's deliverance.

decisions.choice: "through many" goes with the gift: given in answer to many people's prayers
alternatives: "through many" goes with the thanks: many people giving thanks
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves open which phrase "through many" belongs to. Read with the gift, it says the rescue came through the prayers of many, which verse 11 has just mentioned; "from many persons" already covers the thanks. The general sense is the same either way.

decisions.choice: God rescued us; the gift God has given us
alternatives: who rescued us; the gift to us
decisions.reason: The relative pronoun points back to God in verse 9; Balanced and Readable name him because they begin a new sentence. They also name God as the giver of the gift.

decisions.choice: the purpose clause told as a sequence: many pray, God answers, many give thanks
alternatives: so that thanks may be given by many for the gift given through many
decisions.reason: Readable unfolds the compressed Greek clause into steps a young reader can follow.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives (kwake, naye)
alternatives: a span for every English pronoun
decisions.reason: As in Romans and Galatians, Swahili marks most pronouns for God inside the verb ("alituokoa", "atatuokoa", "watamshukuru"), and a verb prefix cannot take a capital. So the setting applies only to free pronouns like "kwake" and "naye", and this letter has fewer spans than the English.

decisions.choice: karama
decisions.reason: "Karama" is a gift given out of God's grace, as in Romans 1:11 and 5:15; here it is God's rescue of Paul (meaning decision).

source.text: Ἡ γὰρ καύχησις ἡμῶν αὕτη ἐστίν, τὸ μαρτύριον τῆς συνειδήσεως ἡμῶν, ὅτι ἐν ἁγιότητι καὶ εἰλικρινείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ, οὐκ ἐν σοφίᾳ σαρκικῇ ἀλλ’ ἐν χάριτι θεοῦ, ἀνεστράφημεν ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, περισσοτέρως δὲ πρὸς ὑμᾶς·

records.literal_gloss: For the boasting of us this is, the testimony of the conscience of us, that in holiness and sincerity of the God, not in wisdom fleshly but in grace of God, we conducted ourselves in the world, and more abundantly toward you;

en.L: For our boasting is this, the testimony of our conscience: that in holiness and sincerity [that come] from God, not in fleshly wisdom but in [the] grace of God, we have conducted ourselves in the world, and all the more toward you.
en.B: Here is what we take pride in, and our conscience confirms it: in the world at large, and still more with you, we have behaved with a holiness and sincerity that come from God, guided not by merely human wisdom but by the grace of God.
en.R: There is one thing we are proud of, and our conscience tells us it is true. Wherever we have been in the world, and most of all with you, we have lived in a holy and honest way that comes from God. We did not depend on human cleverness. We depended on the grace of God.

fr.L: Car notre sujet de fierté, c’est ceci, le témoignage de notre conscience : c’est dans la sainteté et la sincérité [qui viennent] de Dieu, non dans une sagesse de la chair mais dans la grâce de Dieu, que nous nous sommes conduits dans le monde, et plus encore envers vous.
fr.B: Voici ce qui fait notre fierté, et notre conscience en témoigne : dans le monde en général, et plus encore avec vous, nous nous sommes conduits avec une sainteté et une sincérité qui viennent de Dieu, guidés non par une sagesse purement humaine, mais par la grâce de Dieu.
fr.R: Il y a une chose dont nous sommes fiers, et notre conscience nous dit que c’est vrai. Partout où nous sommes allés dans le monde, et surtout chez vous, nous avons vécu d’une manière sainte et honnête, qui vient de Dieu. Nous n’avons pas compté sur l’intelligence humaine. Nous avons compté sur la grâce de Dieu.

es.L: Porque nuestro motivo de gloria es este, el testimonio de nuestra conciencia: que con santidad y sinceridad [que vienen] de Dios, no con sabiduría carnal sino con [la] gracia de Dios, nos hemos conducido en el mundo, y mucho más con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: Esto es lo que nos hace sentirnos orgullosos, y nuestra conciencia lo confirma: en el mundo en general, y todavía más con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, nos hemos comportado con una santidad y una sinceridad que vienen de Dios, guiados no por una sabiduría meramente humana, sino por la gracia de Dios.
es.R: Hay algo de lo que estamos orgullosos, y nuestra conciencia nos dice que es verdad. Dondequiera que hemos estado en el mundo, y sobre todo con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hemos vivido de una manera santa y honesta que viene de Dios. No dependimos de la astucia humana. Dependimos de la gracia de Dios.

sw.L: Kwa maana fahari yetu ni hii, ushuhuda wa dhamiri yetu: kwamba katika utakatifu na unyofu wa Mungu, si katika hekima ya kimwili bali katika neema ya Mungu, tumeenenda ulimwenguni, na zaidi sana kwenu.
sw.B: Hiki ndicho tunachokionea fahari, na dhamiri yetu inathibitisha: ulimwenguni kote, na zaidi sana kwenu ninyi, tumeishi kwa utakatifu na unyofu unaotoka kwa Mungu, tukiongozwa si na hekima ya kibinadamu tu, bali na neema ya Mungu.
sw.R: Kuna jambo moja tunaloona fahari juu yake, na dhamiri yetu inatuambia kwamba ni kweli. Kila mahali tulipokuwa ulimwenguni, na hasa tulipokuwa nanyi, tumeishi maisha matakatifu na ya unyofu yanayotoka kwa Mungu. Hatukutegemea werevu wa kibinadamu. Tulitegemea neema ya Mungu.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "holiness"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts are divided between two Greek words that differ by only a few letters: ἁγιότητι ("holiness") and a word for simplicity, openness of heart. The second fits Paul's language elsewhere in the letter (11:3) and its use with "sincerity"; the first is rarer and is found in important early manuscripts. The SBLGNT prints "holiness". Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: boasting: a proper pride, a ground for confidence
decisions.reason: καύχησις is a key word of 2 Corinthians. Paul condemns boasting in oneself (10:17; 11:18) but here and in 1:14 uses it of a clear conscience and of the people God has given him. The sense is honest pride in what God has done.

decisions.choice: conscience: inner awareness that judges one's own conduct
decisions.reason: συνειδήσεως is the inner witness that approves or condemns what a person has done (Romans 2:15; 2 Corinthians 4:2). Paul's conscience testifies in his favor.

decisions.choice: holiness and sincerity that God gives
decisions.reason: The genitive "of God" most likely marks the source, matching "by the grace of God" in the next phrase: Paul's integrity is God's work in him.

decisions.choice: merely human wisdom: cleverness that works by the world's standards
decisions.reason: σαρκικῇ ("fleshly") describes what is merely human, without God. Paul sets clever speech and calculation against the power of God in 1 Corinthians 1:17-2:5, and in verse 17 of this chapter he will deny planning "according to the flesh".

decisions.choice: merely human wisdom (B); human cleverness (R)
decisions.reason: "Fleshly" suggests the body to a modern reader; Literal keeps it, while Balanced and Readable give the sense. "Worldly" is avoided because "world" in this verse means the world at large, not something bad.

decisions.choice: take pride in (B); are proud of (R)
decisions.reason: In English "boast" is almost always bad. Balanced and Readable use "pride", which can be good or bad, as the Greek word can; Literal keeps "boasting" to show the link with 10:17 and 11:18.

decisions.choice: se vanter, sujet de fierté (L); la fierté, être fier (B, R) (for the whole book; chapters 10-12 keep se vanter at every level)
decisions.reason: Literal always uses the same word so the boasting family can be traced (docs/corinthians-terms.md), and 1 Corinthians and 2 Corinthians 10-13 already say "se vanter", with "sujet de fierté" for Paul's good boast as a noun (11:10). So Literal says "se vanter" and "sujet de fierté" here too, one word across both letters, even though French "se vanter" usually sounds like self-praise and here the word is a proper pride (m2); "sujet de fierté" keeps the noun from sounding bad. "Se glorifier", the established word in some French Bibles, is the alternative. Balanced and Readable say "fierté" and "être fier" where the English says "pride".

decisions.choice: une sagesse de la chair (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "flesh", as the style guide sets, but French "charnel" now suggests the body and sex; "de la chair" keeps Paul's word without that sense. Balanced and Readable give the meaning (m5), as the English does.

decisions.choice: motivo de gloria, gloriarse (L); sentirse orgulloso, motivo de orgullo (B, R)
decisions.reason: Paul speaks here of a proper pride (meaning decision). "Jactarse" always sounds like bragging in Spanish. Literal keeps the traditional "gloriarse / motivo de gloria", as Romans 5 and Galatians 6 do, so the word can be traced; Balanced and Readable say plainly that it is pride, as the English does. In this phrase "gloria" means a reason for pride, not God's glory.

decisions.choice: fahari (noun), kujivunia (verb) at Literal; kuona fahari (B, R)
decisions.reason: Recorded once for the letter. Paul's boasting word is often proper pride (meaning decision). Literal keeps one family for it so the word can be traced: the noun is "fahari", as in Romans 15:17, and the verb "kujivunia", as in Romans 5:2-3. Balanced and Readable say "kuona fahari" (to take pride) where the English does. "Kujisifu" (to praise oneself) and "majivuno" (conceit) always sound bad in Swahili.

decisions.choice: hekima ya kimwili (L); hekima ya kibinadamu tu (B); werevu wa kibinadamu (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the flesh word as an adjective, "ya kimwili"; Balanced and Readable say what it means, merely human wisdom, with "werevu" (cleverness) at Readable.

source.text: οὐ γὰρ ἄλλα γράφομεν ὑμῖν ἀλλ’ ἢ ἃ ἀναγινώσκετε ἢ καὶ ἐπιγινώσκετε, ἐλπίζω δὲ ὅτι ἕως τέλους ἐπιγνώσεσθε, καθὼς καὶ ἐπέγνωτε ἡμᾶς ἀπὸ μέρους, ὅτι καύχημα ὑμῶν ἐσμεν καθάπερ καὶ ὑμεῖς ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: For not other [things] we write to you but than what you read or also understand, and I hope that until [the] end you will understand, \v 14 just as also you understood us in part, that boast of you we are just as also you of us in the day of the Lord of us Jesus.

en.L: For we write nothing else to you than what you read and also understand, and I hope that you will understand fully, \v 14 just as you also did understand us in part, that we are your [reason for] boasting, just as you also [are] ours, on the day of our Lord Jesus.
en.B: We write you nothing other than what you can read and recognize as true. And I hope you will come to recognize it completely, \v 14 as you have already recognized us in part: that we are your reason to be proud, as you are ours, on the day of our Lord Jesus.
en.R: There is nothing hidden in our letters. We mean exactly what you read and understand. I hope you will understand us completely. \v 14 You understand us partly now. But I hope you will see fully that on the day our Lord Jesus comes back, we will be proud of you, and you will be proud of us.

fr.L: Car nous ne vous écrivons pas autre chose que ce que vous lisez et même comprenez, et j’espère que vous comprendrez pleinement, \v 14 comme vous nous avez aussi compris en partie, que nous sommes votre sujet de fierté, comme vous aussi [vous êtes] le nôtre, au jour de notre Seigneur Jésus.
fr.B: Nous ne vous écrivons rien d’autre que ce que vous pouvez lire et reconnaître comme vrai. Et j’espère que vous le reconnaîtrez pleinement, \v 14 comme vous nous avez déjà reconnus en partie : nous sommes pour vous un sujet de fierté, comme vous l’êtes pour nous, au jour de notre Seigneur Jésus.
fr.R: Il n’y a rien de caché dans nos lettres. Nous voulons dire exactement ce que vous lisez et comprenez. J’espère que vous nous comprendrez tout à fait. \v 14 Maintenant, vous nous comprenez en partie. Mais j’espère que vous verrez bien que, le jour où notre Seigneur Jésus reviendra, nous serons fiers de vous, et vous serez fiers de nous.

es.L: Porque no {{plural_you:les|os}} escribimos otras cosas sino lo que {{plural_you:leen|leéis}} y también {{plural_you:entienden|entendéis}}, y espero que {{plural_you:entenderán|entenderéis}} plenamente, \v 14 así como también nos {{plural_you:entendieron|entendisteis}} en parte, que somos {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} motivo de gloria, así como también {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} [{{plural_you:son|sois}}] el nuestro, en el día de nuestro Señor Jesús.
es.B: No {{plural_you:les|os}} escribimos nada distinto de lo que {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} leer y reconocer como verdadero. Y espero que {{plural_you:lleguen|lleguéis}} a reconocerlo plenamente, \v 14 así como ya nos {{plural_you:han reconocido|habéis reconocido}} en parte: que somos para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} motivo de orgullo, como {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} lo {{plural_you:son|sois}} para nosotros, en el día de nuestro Señor Jesús.
es.R: En nuestras cartas no hay nada escondido. Lo que queremos decir es exactamente lo que {{plural_you:leen|leéis}} y {{plural_you:entienden|entendéis}}. Espero que {{plural_you:lleguen|lleguéis}} a entendernos por completo. \v 14 Ahora nos {{plural_you:entienden|entendéis}} en parte. Pero espero que {{plural_you:vean|veáis}} con claridad que, el día en que nuestro Señor Jesús vuelva, nosotros estaremos orgullosos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y {{plural_you:ustedes estarán|vosotros estaréis}} orgullosos de nosotros.

sw.L: Kwa maana hatuwaandikii mambo mengine isipokuwa yale mnayoyasoma na pia kuyaelewa, na natumaini kwamba mtaelewa kikamilifu, \v 14 kama vile mlivyotuelewa kwa sehemu, kwamba sisi ni fahari yenu, kama vile ninyi pia [mlivyo fahari] yetu, katika siku ya Bwana wetu Yesu.
sw.B: Hatuwaandikii jambo lingine lolote zaidi ya yale mnayoweza kuyasoma na kuyatambua kuwa kweli. Na natumaini mtayatambua kikamilifu, \v 14 kama vile mmekwisha kututambua kwa sehemu: kwamba sisi ni sababu yenu ya kuona fahari, kama ninyi mlivyo sababu yetu, katika siku ya Bwana wetu Yesu.
sw.R: Hakuna jambo lililofichwa katika barua zetu. Tunamaanisha hasa yale mnayosoma na kuelewa. Natumaini mtatuelewa kikamilifu. \v 14 Sasa mnatuelewa kwa sehemu tu. Lakini natumaini mtaona wazi kwamba siku ile Bwana wetu Yesu atakaporudi, sisi tutaona fahari juu yenu, nanyi mtaona fahari juu yetu.

decisions.choice: no hidden meaning: Paul's letters mean what they plainly say
alternatives: a general remark about clear writing
decisions.reason: Paul plays on two similar verbs, ἀναγινώσκετε ("you read") and ἐπιγινώσκετε ("you recognize, understand"). He is answering a charge that his letters say one thing and he means another (compare 10:9-11). There is nothing "other" behind what the Corinthians read.

decisions.choice: fully: to the point of complete understanding
alternatives: until the end: until the day of the Lord
decisions.reason: ἕως τέλους can mean "completely" or "until the end". Set against "in part" in verse 14, "fully" fits; but the mention of the day of the Lord at the end of verse 14 makes "until the end" possible.

decisions.choice: in part: they understand Paul only partly
decisions.reason: ἀπὸ μέρους can mean "partly" or "some of you". Paul uses it for partial understanding in 1 Corinthians 13:9-12; but the letter also shows that some in Corinth were against him (2:5-6; 10:10), so the other reading is possible.

decisions.choice: a reason for boasting: someone to be proud of
decisions.reason: καύχημα is the ground of boasting, used in a good sense as in Philippians 2:16: on the day of the Lord, Paul and the church will each be the other's reason for pride before Christ.

decisions.choice: the day of Christ's return
decisions.reason: The prophets spoke of "the day of the Lord" (Amos 5:18; Joel 2:31). Paul applies it to the Lord Jesus, whose coming he awaits (1 Corinthians 1:8; Philippians 1:6).

decisions.choice: recognize
decisions.reason: The verb means both to understand and to acknowledge. Balanced uses "recognize", which has both senses; Literal and Readable use "understand".

decisions.choice: There is nothing hidden in our letters. We mean exactly what you read
alternatives: We write you nothing other than what you read
decisions.reason: Readable states the point Paul is making against the charge of double meaning (see the meaning decision), and names the return of the Lord Jesus as the day meant.

source.text: Καὶ ταύτῃ τῇ πεποιθήσει ἐβουλόμην πρότερον πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐλθεῖν, ἵνα δευτέραν χάριν σχῆτε, καὶ δι’ ὑμῶν διελθεῖν εἰς Μακεδονίαν, καὶ πάλιν ἀπὸ Μακεδονίας ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ ὑφ’ ὑμῶν προπεμφθῆναι εἰς τὴν Ἰουδαίαν.

records.literal_gloss: And in this confidence I was wanting formerly to you to come, so that a second grace you might have, \v 16 and through you to pass through into Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come to you and by you to be sent on into the Judea.

en.L: And with this confidence I wanted to come to you first, so that you might have a second grace, \v 16 and to pass through you into Macedonia, and to come again from Macedonia to you, and to be sent on by you to Judea.
en.B: Confident of this, I had planned to come to you first, to give you a second gift of grace. \v 16 I would pass through your city on the way to Macedonia, return to you from Macedonia, and then let you help me on my journey to Judea.
en.R: I was sure about this, so I made a plan to visit you first. That way you would receive God's grace twice, through two visits from me. \v 16 I planned to stop with you on my way to Macedonia. Then I would come back to you from Macedonia, and you would help me on my trip to Judea.

fr.L: Et avec cette assurance, je voulais d’abord venir chez vous, afin que vous ayez une seconde grâce, \v 16 et passer par chez vous [pour aller] en Macédoine, et de Macédoine revenir chez vous, et être mis en route par vous vers la Judée.
fr.B: Fort de cette assurance, j’avais projeté de venir d’abord chez vous, pour vous apporter un second don de grâce. \v 16 Je voulais passer par votre ville en allant en Macédoine, revenir chez vous depuis la Macédoine, puis vous laisser m’aider à poursuivre mon voyage vers la Judée.
fr.R: J’en étais sûr, alors j’avais fait le projet de venir d’abord vous voir. Ainsi, vous auriez reçu deux fois la grâce de Dieu, par deux visites de ma part. \v 16 Je voulais m’arrêter chez vous en allant en Macédoine. Ensuite, je serais revenu chez vous depuis la Macédoine, et vous m’auriez aidé pour mon voyage en Judée.

es.L: Y con esta confianza quería ir primero a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, para que {{plural_you:tuvieran|tuvierais}} una segunda gracia, \v 16 y pasar por [donde {{plural_you:están|estáis}}] hacia Macedonia, y de nuevo desde Macedonia ir a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y ser encaminado por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} a Judea.
es.B: Confiando en esto, había planeado {{plural_you:visitarlos|visitaros}} primero, para que {{plural_you:recibieran|recibierais}} un segundo don de la gracia. \v 16 Pasaría por {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} ciudad de camino a Macedonia, volvería a {{plural_you:visitarlos|visitaros}} al regresar de Macedonia, y luego {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} me {{plural_you:ayudarían|ayudaríais}} a seguir mi viaje a Judea.
es.R: Yo estaba seguro de esto, así que hice planes para {{plural_you:visitarlos|visitaros}} primero. De esa manera {{plural_you:recibirían|recibiríais}} la gracia de Dios dos veces, por medio de dos visitas mías. \v 16 Pensaba pasar a {{plural_you:verlos|veros}} de camino a Macedonia. Después volvería a {{plural_you:visitarlos|visitaros}} al regresar de Macedonia, y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} me {{plural_you:ayudarían|ayudaríais}} en mi viaje a Judea.

sw.L: Na kwa uhakika huu nilitaka kuja kwenu kwanza, ili mpate neema ya pili, \v 16 na kupitia kwenu kwenda Makedonia, na tena kutoka Makedonia kuja kwenu, na kusafirishwa nanyi kwenda Yudea.
sw.B: Nikiwa na uhakika huu, nilikuwa nimepanga kuja kwenu kwanza, ili mpate karama ya pili ya neema. \v 16 Ningepita katika mji wenu nikienda Makedonia, kisha nirudi kwenu kutoka Makedonia, nanyi mnisaidie katika safari yangu kwenda Yudea.
sw.R: Nilikuwa na uhakika juu ya jambo hili, kwa hiyo nilipanga kuwatembelea ninyi kwanza. Kwa njia hiyo mngepokea neema ya Mungu mara mbili, kupitia ziara zangu mbili. \v 16 Nilipanga kukaa nanyi nikiwa njiani kwenda Makedonia. Kisha ningerudi kwenu kutoka Makedonia, nanyi mngenisaidia katika safari yangu ya kwenda Yudea.

decisions.choice: a second gift of God's grace, brought through a second visit
alternatives: a second favor or kindness from Paul
a second chance to show kindness
decisions.reason: χάριν here is not God's grace in the general sense but a particular benefit of it: Paul's visits bring God's gifts (Romans 1:11; 15:29). The plan was to visit Corinth twice, before and after Macedonia, so "second" means a second visit and its blessing.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "grace"
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read a similar Greek word meaning "joy", which differs by one letter and fits the mention of joy in verse 24 and 2:3. The SBLGNT follows the reading "grace", found in most early manuscripts. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: first: before going to Macedonia
alternatives: earlier: at an earlier time, before the plan changed
decisions.reason: πρότερον can mean "first" in a sequence or "earlier" in time. Verse 16 sets out the order of the trip: Corinth, Macedonia, Corinth again. Either reading fits the plan that was dropped.

decisions.choice: Paul's changed travel plans
decisions.reason: In 1 Corinthians 16:5-7 Paul planned to go through Macedonia and then come to Corinth. Here he describes a later plan, a double visit. He did not carry it out (1:23; 2:1), and his critics used the change against him. Judea was the goal because he was taking the collection to the believers in Jerusalem (1 Corinthians 16:1-4; Romans 15:25-26). Macedonia was the province north of Achaia, with Philippi and Thessalonica.

decisions.choice: to be sent on: helped on a journey with supplies and company
decisions.reason: προπεμφθῆναι was the regular word for a church's help to a traveling preacher: food, money, sometimes companions (Romans 15:24; 1 Corinthians 16:6; Titus 3:13).

decisions.choice: a second gift of grace (B); receive God's grace twice, through two visits from me (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the "second grace" was (see the meaning decision) and keep the key word "grace".

decisions.choice: pass through your city (B); stop with you (R)
decisions.reason: "Through you" means through Corinth, where they live.

decisions.choice: être mis en route par vous (L)
decisions.reason: "Être envoyé" would suggest that the church sends Paul on a mission; the verb means helping a traveller on his way with supplies and company (m5). "Mettre en route" says that without leaving Literal; Balanced and Readable say the help plainly.

decisions.choice: un segundo don de la gracia
decisions.reason: "Gracia" stays as the key term; "don" says that the second visit would bring them God's gift of grace (meaning decision), not a favor from Paul.

decisions.choice: kusafirishwa nanyi (L); mnisaidie katika safari yangu (B, R)
decisions.reason: To be sent on was to be given supplies and company for the road (meaning decision). Literal keeps the passive "kusafirishwa" (to be sent on one's way); Balanced and Readable say what the Corinthians would do. "Kusindikizwa" (to be escorted) names only the company.

source.text: τοῦτο οὖν βουλόμενος μήτι ἄρα τῇ ἐλαφρίᾳ ἐχρησάμην;

records.literal_gloss: This therefore wanting, [did] I then use the lightness?

en.L: So when I wanted this, did I really act with lightness?
en.B: So when I planned this, did I treat it lightly?
en.R: When I planned all this, I was not careless about it, was I?

fr.L: En voulant donc cela, ai-je donc agi avec légèreté ?
fr.B: Quand j’ai fait ce projet, l’ai-je donc pris à la légère ?
fr.R: Quand j’ai fait tous ces projets, je ne les ai pas faits à la légère, n’est-ce pas ?

es.L: Así que, queriendo esto, ¿acaso actué con ligereza?
es.B: Entonces, cuando planeé esto, ¿lo tomé a la ligera?
es.R: Cuando hice todos estos planes, no fui descuidado, ¿verdad?

sw.L: Basi nilipotaka hili, je, kweli nilitenda kwa wepesi?
sw.B: Basi nilipopanga hivyo, je, nililichukulia jambo hilo kwa wepesi?
sw.R: Nilipopanga hayo yote, sikuwa mzembe, sivyo?

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer "no"
decisions.reason: μήτι introduces a question to which the speaker expects a negative answer. Paul is not unsure; he is rejecting a charge.

decisions.choice: lightness: fickleness, making plans carelessly and dropping them
decisions.reason: ἐλαφρίᾳ means lightness, here in the sense of being unreliable. The article ("the lightness") may point to the very fickleness the Corinthians had accused him of.

decisions.choice: I was not careless about it, was I?
decisions.reason: A tag question shows young readers that the expected answer is "no", as the Greek does.

decisions.choice: kwa wepesi
decisions.reason: "Wepesi" is lightness, the Greek picture; with "kutenda" or "kuchukulia" it means treating a matter lightly. "Kigeugeu" (fickleness) would say the same plainly and is close to the "Ndiyo, ndiyo" and "Hapana, hapana" of the next sentence.

source.text: ἢ ἃ βουλεύομαι κατὰ σάρκα βουλεύομαι, ἵνα ᾖ παρ’ ἐμοὶ τὸ Ναὶ ναὶ καὶ τὸ Οὒ οὔ;

records.literal_gloss: Or what I plan, according to flesh do I plan, so that there may be with me the Yes yes and the No no?

en.L: Or what I plan, do I plan according to [the] flesh, so that with me there may be "Yes, yes" and "No, no"?
en.B: Or are my plans made by merely human standards, so that with me it is "Yes, yes" and "No, no" at once?
en.R: Do I make plans the way selfish people do? Do I say "Yes, yes" and then "No, no" whenever it suits me?

fr.L: Ou ce que je projette, est-ce selon la chair que je le projette, de sorte qu’il y ait chez moi le « Oui, oui » et le « Non, non » ?
fr.B: Ou bien mes projets sont-ils faits selon des critères purement humains, de sorte que chez moi ce soit à la fois « Oui, oui » et « Non, non » ?
fr.R: Est-ce que je fais des projets comme les gens égoïstes ? Est-ce que je dis « Oui, oui » puis « Non, non », selon ce qui m’arrange ?

es.L: ¿O lo que planeo, lo planeo según [la] carne, para que haya en mí el «Sí, sí» y el «No, no»?
es.B: ¿O hago mis planes con criterios meramente humanos, de modo que conmigo es «Sí, sí» y «No, no» a la vez?
es.R: ¿Hago planes como lo hace la gente egoísta? ¿Digo «Sí, sí» y luego «No, no» cuando me conviene?

sw.L: Au mambo ninayoyapanga, je, nayapanga kwa kufuata mwili, ili kwangu kuwe na "Ndiyo, ndiyo" na "Hapana, hapana"?
sw.B: Au je, mipango yangu inafanywa kwa vipimo vya kibinadamu tu, hata kwangu iwe "Ndiyo, ndiyo" na "Hapana, hapana" wakati mmoja?
sw.R: Je, mimi hupanga mambo kama watu wenye ubinafsi wanavyofanya? Je, nasema "Ndiyo, ndiyo" kisha "Hapana, hapana" kila inaponifaa?

decisions.choice: by merely human standards: planning for one's own advantage
decisions.reason: κατὰ σάρκα describes plans made the way people do without God, shaped by self-interest. Some in Corinth said Paul lived this way (10:2); he answers the charge here and in verse 12.

decisions.choice: saying yes and no about the same thing: being unreliable
alternatives: an emphatic yes that truly means yes
decisions.reason: Elsewhere a doubled "yes" means a plain, honest yes (Matthew 5:37; James 5:12). Here, with "yes, yes" and "no, no" both "with me", the picture is of a man whose answer can be either, so that no one can rely on his word. Verse 18 confirms this: his word is not "Yes and No".

decisions.choice: by merely human standards (B); the way selfish people do (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 12, Literal keeps "flesh", while Balanced and Readable give the sense.

decisions.choice: at once (B); then ... whenever it suits me (R)
decisions.reason: These words make clear that the doubled yes and no describe unreliability, not emphasis (see the meaning decision).

source.text: πιστὸς δὲ ὁ θεὸς ὅτι ὁ λόγος ἡμῶν ὁ πρὸς ὑμᾶς οὐκ ἔστιν Ναὶ καὶ Οὔ.

records.literal_gloss: But faithful [is] the God, that the word of us the [one] to you is not Yes and No.

en.L: But God [is] faithful, that our word to you is not "Yes and No."
en.B: But God is faithful, and our word to you is not "Yes" and "No" at once.
en.R: God is faithful. And just as surely, what we say to you does not mean "Yes" and "No" at the same time.

fr.L: Mais Dieu [est] fidèle : notre parole adressée à vous n’est pas « Oui et Non ».
fr.B: Mais Dieu est fidèle, et notre parole pour vous n’est pas à la fois « Oui » et « Non ».
fr.R: Dieu est fidèle. Et c’est aussi sûr que cela : ce que nous vous disons ne veut pas dire « Oui » et « Non » en même temps.

es.L: Pero fiel [es] Dios, que nuestra palabra a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no es «Sí y No».
es.B: Pero Dios es fiel, y nuestra palabra a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no es «Sí» y «No» a la vez.
es.R: Dios es fiel. Y con la misma seguridad, lo que {{plural_you:les|os}} decimos no significa «Sí» y «No» al mismo tiempo.

sw.L: Lakini Mungu [ni] mwaminifu, kwamba neno letu kwenu si "Ndiyo na Hapana."
sw.B: Lakini Mungu ni mwaminifu, na neno letu kwenu si "Ndiyo" na "Hapana" wakati mmoja.
sw.R: Mungu ni mwaminifu. Na kwa hakika hiyo hiyo, maneno tunayowaambia hayamaanishi "Ndiyo" na "Hapana" kwa wakati mmoja.

decisions.choice: a form of oath: as surely as God is faithful
alternatives: a statement with a reason: God is faithful, because our word is not yes and no
decisions.reason: The phrase is like "God is my witness" (verse 23; Romans 1:9). Paul appeals to God's faithfulness to back his own: he is God's messenger, and God is not unreliable.
